kernel.governing_law: The speaker asserts knowledge without authority — prophecy disclaimed as prophecy, certitude offered from an empty credential — and stakes that the resourceful captive will overcome constraint by native cunning, while demanding the listener prove his own lineage through speech.
kernel.mutated_relation: The conditions of the utterance surfaced as the utterance itself: the captive is held because holding is what permits prophecy; the disclaimer of authority is the authority; the demand for proof of lineage is the confession that the speaker's own words require the listener's identity to become true.

independent.recovered_law: In Text A, Odysseus is a real agent held physically captive whose return depends on his own cunning and the gods' will, while in Text B, Odysseus exists only as a function of the narrative act itself — his captivity, return, and identity are reconstituted as effects of the speech that tells them, so that the relation between character and story is inverted from 'story describes agent' to 'speech constitutes its subject.'
independent.law_match_note: Both describe the same structural inversion: conditions/mechanisms of narration (captivity, authority, identity) collapse into the narration itself, so that what was described becomes constituted by the act of description — the relation between utterance and its subject is inverted from representational to constitutive.
independent.terminal_note: The final lines (206–207) maintain the inversion: the listener must ground the speech's truth (206) and is defined as the speech's 'one possible listener' (207), sustaining the constitutive-speech relation throughout.
